setup_summary.text: The next report is fiscal Q4 2026, due 2027-01-25 after the close. Consensus is EPS of $2.29 and revenue of $113.43B. The EPS basis (GAAP or adjusted) is not specified.

Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-13: revenue $112.7B, earnings from operations $6.6B, GAAP diluted EPS $4.56 and adjusted EPS $4.69. Adjusted EPS was $2.92 a year earlier. Q3 operating earnings were down from $8.0B in Q2 (Q2 GAAP EPS was $6.04), a seasonal step-down as medical costs rise in the second half.
Q3 adjusted EPS of $4.69 beat the Zacks consensus of $4.12, and revenue beat by about 1.2%. This comes from a news article, not the filings.

Management raised FY2026 guidance to GAAP EPS of at least $19.50 and adjusted EPS of at least $20.50. Nine-month EPS was $17.50 GAAP and $18.30 adjusted, so the guidance implies Q4 EPS of at least about $2.00 GAAP and about $2.20 adjusted. Consensus of $2.29 sits only about $0.09 above the adjusted floor.

The guidance implies a sharp Q4 step down. Projected FY adjusted net earnings of more than $18,585M, less $16,598M for nine months, leave at least about $1.99B for Q4. Q3 adjusted net earnings were $4.23B. Management cited H2 utilization seasonality, and Optum Health cited Q4 risk seasonality and added investments.

The 2027 outlook is expected before year-end, ahead of the Jan-25 print. Management says $20.50 is a 'solid run rate', consensus 2027 'may understate the opportunity', and the low end of the 13%-16% growth range is a reasonable starting point.

The year-ago Q4 comparison base is distorted. Q4 2025 operating earnings were about $0.38B (FY $18,964M less nine-month $18,584M, derived). Q4 2025 carried about $2.5B of restructuring and other actions plus a $799M cyberattack loan reserve. Derived Q4 2025 revenue was about $113.2B, so consensus revenue is about +0.2% year on year. The fact-sheet 'consensus-implied' growth rows (F.70, F.72) compare against Q3 2025, not Q4 2025, and should not be used.

Market positioning: the stock is $406.97 against a consensus price target of $478.68 (+17.6%). The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±8.1%. UNH beat in 3 of the last 4 quarters, with an average surprise of +12.3%. No options-implied move or whisper number is available yet.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $4.69 (GAAP $4.56), with $610M of net favorable reserve development in the quarter.

view.text: The guidance floor implies adjusted EPS of at least about $2.20, so consensus is roughly 4% above the floor. 'At least' wording and the Q3 beat argue for a modest beat. Q4 seasonality and added investments argue against a large one. The result will hinge on Q4 MCR and any further favorable reserve development.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 revenue was $112.694B, down about 0.4% year on year.

view.text: Consensus implies about +0.65% sequentially despite shrinking membership: UnitedHealthcare served 48.3M at Sep 30 versus 48.5M at Jun 30. Medicare Advantage has contracted 935K since year-end and Optum Health revenue fell 10% year on year in Q3. Revenue upside looks limited. Derived Q4 2025 revenue was about $113.2B.

last_reported.text: Q3 MCR was 88.4% versus 89.9% a year earlier and 86.7% in Q2. Q4 2025 MCR was about 92.4% (derived), which included a $623M loss-contract reserve.

view.text: Expect a seasonal rise from 88.4%, which management flagged for risk-based businesses. On roughly $87B of quarterly premiums, each 100bp of MCR is about $0.87B pre-tax, or about $0.75 per share after tax at about 22% (our arithmetic). Q3 benefited from $610M of favorable development, so any fade is a downside risk.

last_reported.text: Q3 operating cost ratio was 12.8% versus 13.5% a year earlier.

view.text: Management plans to 'accelerate' investments in the final months of 2026. They also expect heavier 2027 investment in policy reform and modernization, especially at UnitedHealthcare and Optum Insight. Risk skews to a higher ratio than Q3.

last_reported.text: Q3 UnitedHealthcare operating earnings were $2.83B (3.3% margin) versus $1.8B (2.1%) a year earlier; Q2 was $3.9B (4.6%).

view.text: Management says the Medicare margin is now near the top of the 2%-4% range and 2026 core Medicaid margin is moderately better than -1%. Commercial trend is above 11%, though stabilizing. Q4 is likely lower than Q3 on seasonality, and commercial is the swing factor.

last_reported.text: Q3 operating earnings were $735M (3.2% margin) on revenue of $22.9B, down 10% year on year. A year earlier earnings were $41M (0.2%).

view.text: An analyst said guidance implies a 'meaningfully negative' Q4. Management attributed this to risk seasonality and added technology, AI and workflow investments, and said Q3 performance is durable. Target margin is 6%-8% by 2028. Watch for a possible Q4 loss as the key swing item.

metrics_to_model.metric: Optum Rx adjusted scripts and earnings

last_reported.text: Q3 adjusted scripts were 393M versus 414M a year earlier, down about 5%. Earnings from operations were $1.7B (4.3% margin) versus $1.5B. Specialty volume was up 2.6%.

view.text: Scripts are tied to UnitedHealthcare membership declines. Over 50% of Optum Rx membership is now external. Earnings growth rests on biosimilars and specialty mix, with a 100% rebate pass-through commitment coming by Jan 2028.

metrics_to_model.metric: UnitedHealthcare people served and Medicare Advantage membership

last_reported.text: At Sep 30, UnitedHealthcare medical membership was 48.3M (Dec 31, 2025: 49.76M). Medicare Advantage was 7.605M, up from 7.565M at Jun 30 but down from 8.445M at year-end.

view.text: Annual enrollment begins mid-October. Management will give formal 2027 membership guidance later in the year and has signalled focus on D-SNP, C-SNP and HMO plans. The Q4 year-end count is a read on retention.

last_reported.text: Days claims payable were 47.0 (flat versus Q2, 46.2 a year ago). Debt-to-capital was 41.7% at Sep 30 versus 41.2% at Jun 30. The target is about 40% by year-end. Year-to-date dividends were $6.2B and buybacks $5.0B.

view.text: Management expects dividends above $8B for 2026 and to approach 40% debt-to-capital by year-end. Reserve adequacy (days claims payable) is the quality check on any Q4 medical-cost beat.

since_filing.text: Since the Aug 10 10-Q, Q3 results showed operating earnings of $6.6B versus $4.3B a year earlier, and the MCR fell to 88.4% from 89.9%. Operating earnings were down from $8.0B in Q2, and the MCR rose from 86.7% in Q2.
Guidance was raised on Oct 13 to at least $20.50 adjusted EPS. Management called it a 'solid run rate' and said it would give a more complete 2027 outlook before year-end.

Q3 included $610M of net favorable reserve development. This is the earnings-quality item to watch. The 10-Q showed $1.25B of favorable prior-year development in H1. The Q3 release describes the $610M as 'related to 2026 dates of service', so its comparability with the 10-Q prior-year figure is unclear.

The call added trend detail not in the 10-Q. Commercial trend is above the initial 11% expectation and still tracking north of 11%. No Surprises Act arbitration awards can approach nearly 6% of total medical spend in some regions.
2027 Medicare Advantage Star results had at least 69% of members in 4+ Star plans, in line with expectations. Management expects to approach 75% as it moves into 2028.

A $1B commitment to the United Health Foundation was disclosed, and the company committed to 100% pass-through of manufacturer rebate discounts to clients by January 1, 2028. The 10-Q had already shown a $400M Foundation contribution in H1.

After the print, sell-side rating actions through 2026-10-27 were all maintained: Overweight/Outperform at Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Mizuho, RBC, Bernstein, JP Morgan, Piper and Barclays, and Hold/Neutral at TD Cowen and Baird.
Debt fell: long-term debt was $68.7B at Sep 30 versus $69.5B at Jun 30. The $3B health care acquisition closed Jul 2 for $1.5B in cash, with $1.5B payable within a year.

key_debates.question: Is the Q4 guidance floor conservative, or is Q3 inflated by reserve releases?

bull.text: Management called at least $20.50 a 'solid run rate', and Q3 adjusted EPS beat the Zacks consensus by about $0.57. The floor implies a Q4 decline that is largely seasonal.

bear.text: Q3 included $610M of favorable reserve development, about $0.5 per share after tax (our arithmetic). Q4 2025 MCR was about 92.4%, and management says it is 'respectful' of H2 utilization and plans accelerated investments.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 MCR, prior-period development and days claims payable in the Jan-25 release, versus the roughly $2.20 implied adjusted EPS floor.

key_debates.question: Will commercial risk margins recover, or does the No Surprises Act and trend keep pressure on?

bull.text: Commercial trend is stabilizing, and 2027 pricing assumes the elevated trends persist. National account persistency looks strong.

bear.text: Trend is still above 11%, arbitration awards run at 10-11x Medicare in some cases, and management said the margin recovery will 'stretch out'.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 commercial MCR commentary, the 2027 outlook and 2027 commercial pricing/selling-season results.

key_debates.question: Can 2027 EPS growth start at the low end of 13%-16%, or does investment and funding pressure cap it?

bull.text: Management sees tailwinds from buybacks, value-based care and AI productivity, and says consensus may understate the opportunity. 13% on $20.50 is about $23.2.

bear.text: Management also flagged accelerating investments in policy reform and modernization, with health benefit funding still pressured. Forward consensus EPS of $22.69 (Forbes, next-12-months, basis unclear) is already close to the implied level.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 2027 outlook promised before year-end and the Jan-25 call.

key_debates.question: Is the Optum Health turnaround durable given the implied Q4 loss?

bull.text: Q3 operating earnings were $735M versus $41M a year ago, and management says the improvement is durable and 2027 earnings will grow.

bear.text: Revenue fell 10% on fewer value-based patients, and an analyst said guidance implies a meaningfully negative Q4. The loss-contract reserve releases, which are excluded from adjusted results, help GAAP.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Optum Health operating earnings and the 2027 margin walk toward 6%-8%.

Days claims payable falls from 47.0 or adverse prior-period development
Optum Health records a larger Q4 loss
Medicare Advantage retention weaker than expected through annual enrollment

claim.text: Medical cost trend and reserve estimation: the 10-K flags that small differences between predicted and actual costs can swing results materially. A 1% IBNR error was about $300M of net earnings at year-end 2025. Q3 benefited from $610M of favorable development.
No Surprises Act arbitration (IDR) cost inflation in commercial: awards can approach nearly 6% of total medical spend in some regions, and trend is above 11%.

Medicare Advantage funding and regulation: the 2027 final rate notice moved toward but remained below industry trend, and risk adjustment revisions continue. RADV audits and the DOJ False Claims Act case, where the DOJ asked the court to reject a Special Master's recommendation for summary judgment in the company's favor, remain unresolved.

IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment for 2017-2020 intercompany transfer pricing with a foreign subsidiary seek to 'significantly increase taxable income'. The company disputes them and considers its reserves adequate. This was received after the 10-K was signed.

Medicaid rate timing: state rate updates lag acuity, and eligibility reductions and the exit from one state continue to shrink membership. Margin recovery to targeted levels is not expected until 2028.

Optum Rx volume and model change: adjusted scripts fell about 5% year on year as UnitedHealthcare membership shrank. The transparent fee-based PBM model and 100% rebate pass-through by 2028 alter economics.

Credit and capital: senior debt carries Negative outlooks at Moody's, S&P and Fitch. Debt-to-capital is 41.7% against a target of about 40%, and the 10-Q carries $1.9B of unrealized losses on available-for-sale debt securities.

Portfolio and one-time items affect GAAP-to-adjusted bridges: the remaining South American sale is still pending with ongoing losses ($76M in Q3). The loss-contract reserve decrease and Foundation funding flow through GAAP and adjusted differently.
